meta.no_manufactured_pit: No historical point-in-time observation can be manufactured. Every ACTUAL_OBSERVATION claim in this study must name a concrete sync_run/observation row; where none exists the time basis is HISTORICAL_PROXY, SOURCE_PUBLISHED, DATE_ONLY or TIME_UNKNOWN.

clinicaltrials_gov.historical_state_conclusion: API v2 exposes exactly one registry state per study: the current one. There is no version/history endpoint; unknown as-of parameters are either rejected or silently ignored (byte-identical response). Only lastUpdatePostDate is offered as a time filter, and it is a stamp on the current record, not a pointer into a retrievable past state. Therefore no historical point-in-time registry state can be recovered from this source.

europe_pmc.historical_state_conclusion: Europe PMC search returns the CURRENT indexed record only. dateOfCreation and dateOfRevision describe the metadata record's own history, not a retrievable snapshot; there is no as-of query parameter. firstIndexDate is the best available SOURCE_PUBLISHED proxy for 'available in this index', and it is measured to lag the journal publication date by the amount tabulated.

openalex.budget_note: hard cap: <=8 requests total for this source
openalex.historical_state_conclusion: OpenAlex returns a single current version of each work: publication_date (science), created_date (when the OpenAlex record was inserted) and updated_date (last index refresh). updated_date overwrites, it does not preserve history, and no as-of/versioned query exists. Under the shared daily budget this was only probed at the record level.

crossref.created_meaning: 'created' is the moment Crossref registered the DOI record (the publisher's deposit / metadata registration time). It is an infrastructure timestamp: it is neither the scientific event, nor the journal publication date, and it is most certainly not an observation by MedRadar. 'deposited' is the last metadata deposit and therefore moves forward; it does not preserve history.
crossref.historical_state_conclusion: Crossref /works/<doi> returns the latest deposit for the DOI. There is no as-of parameter that reconstructs an earlier metadata state; 'created' is immutable per DOI but carries no scientific-event semantics.

contradictions.published_before_event_ctgov_note: For a trial, event_at=startDate and published_at=studyFirstPostDate. A negative value means the trial was registered BEFORE it started, which is pre-registration and legitimate, not an anachronism.
contradictions.published_before_event_europepmc_note: For a publication, published_at=firstIndexDate and event_at=firstPublicationDate; a negative value would mean the record was indexed before the paper was published (a real contradiction).

event_at_after_audit_date.note: event_at later than the audit date is a planned start / estimated completion. It cannot be evidence that anything happened yet.

genuine_actual_observation.definition: A row carries ACTUAL_OBSERVATION evidence iff its first_seen_at is anchored to a real sync_run row that has a start timestamp (proof a collection actually happened), the observation is not a backfill, and the lag first_seen_at - published_at is small enough to be prospective (<=1 day).
genuine_actual_observation.warning: first_seen_at for all 400 rows was built by observation_phase.method='reconstructed_from_run_history', i.e. it is assigned from the sync_run start timestamp AFTER the run, not stamped at the instant the record was written. Resolution is therefore the run start second, and the value is an honest reconstruction of a real collection, not an independently captured per-record timestamp.

s028_comparison.verdict_sentence: The observation ledger is byte-for-byte the same situation S-028 reported: the same 400 observations, the same single day of collection history, the same 6 prospective observations. Nothing improved and nothing regressed - because no new collection cycle has happened.

claims_clock_completeness.strict_definition: first_seen_at value present in the observation ledger AND lag(first_seen_at - published_at) <= 1 day

first_seen_clock_family.reading: the ledger holds a handful of run-anchored timestamps and stopped at its last sync_run; the claims carry many more distinct, later values. So claim-level first_seen_at is the extraction-run write time, not an observation recorded by the observation ledger. Those are two different clock families and must not be presented as the same evidence.

strict_vs_lenient.strict_definition: first_seen_at value exists in the observation ledger AND lag(first_seen_at - published_at) <= 1 day
strict_vs_lenient.lenient_definition: 0 <= lag(first_seen_at - published_at) <= 7 days, using whatever first_seen_at the extract stored; it does NOT require the timestamp to come from the observation ledger
strict_vs_lenient.reading: The strict number is the STUDY'S VERDICT and is 0: no claim carries a point-in-time observation. The lenient number counts claims whose extraction stamp happens to fall within a week of the published date; that is a statement about this study's own fetch, not about knowledge available at the time. Reporting both is correct only if the lenient label is never called an observation.

pipeline_fields_audit.reading: The pipeline's own strict flag is audited, not trusted: this audit re-derives strictness from the observation ledger for every claim and reports any disagreement in both directions.

references_publication_temporal_audit.reading: The ClinicalTrials.gov reference list is CURRENT-STATE: the registry keeps no history of when a reference was added, and the only stamp is lastUpdatePostDate. A trial first posted in 2012 that lists a 2026 paper therefore means the reference was added at a later registry update - it is back-dating of the relation, not a contradiction. The claim dates the citation by the TRIAL's first-post date, which is the defect. A cited paper published in an EARLIER year is legitimate, but the relation must then be dated by the paper's date, not by the trial's.

claims_clock_completeness.downstream_statement: Edges built from these claims are SOURCE_PUBLISHED or HISTORICAL_PROXY unless the claim carries a first_seen_at that the observation ledger actually contains with lag <= 1 day; the measured count is in actual_observation_support.n_strict_genuine.

any_source.note: valid_from / valid_to is present in NO source API; only the all_sources row reserves it, marked HISTORICAL_PROXY and derived.

study_corpus_precision_audit.note: reads the study's own extract files read-only; nothing is written to them and no network call is made
study_corpus_precision_audit.reading: The extractor preserves source precision (month-only source values stay month-only; nothing is silently promoted to a day). But the per-record first_seen_at in these files is a near-unique sub-second value inside a few-second window - the ETL write clock - not an observation recorded by the observation ledger, whose clock stopped earlier and has only a handful of distinct values. These are two different clock families.
